Mercury tidal locking — the 3:2 spin-orbit capture

The simulated history of Mercury: tidal braking from an 11.6-hour day, capture into the 3:2 spin-orbit resonance at 4.65 million simulated years (time compression x1000), locked ever after. Final year 87.96776 d (observed 87.969), rotation 58.65118 d (observed 58.646), solar day 175.98956 d (observed 175.938). Capture odds measured by a 64-branch phase sweep: 5 of 64 branches captured. Playback replays recorded SUNDIALS CVODE samples; the orbit panel animates the recorded orbit shape and spin ratio at display speed (not real time).

Space = play/pause, arrows = step
